description:
MEASURED, and it dwarfs everything else currently ticketed on compile cost. This is the answer to "why does a small program fire so many events".

THE FLOOR IS FINE. The runtime library is genuinely lazy -- nothing is compiled that is not reached:
  main with dbg(1)                   80 jobs,   88 settles,   4 executables, 0.05s
  main with dbg(1 + 2 * 3)          166 jobs,  182 settles,   8 executables, 0.06s
  one Enum.find call site           290 jobs,  475 settles,  16 executables, 0.18s

THE SLOPE IS NOT. A ladder of n identical call sites, each dbg(Enum.find(xs, lambda)):
  n    secs   jobs  settles  execs   exec/site
  1    0.18    290      477     16
  2    0.24    318      734     23      +7
  4    0.32    368     1207     37      +7
  8    0.49    467     2150     65      +7
  16   1.09    672     4038    121      +7
  32   3.33   1091     7846    233      +7
SEVEN executables and ~245 product settles per additional call site.

WHERE THEY COME FROM (backend dump, find_4): 35 executables, only 17 distinct (function, need). SIX functions -- fn66, fn72, fn99, fn162, fn170, fn174 -- have exactly one executable PER CALL SITE, each with a DISTINCT arrow Ty. 6 x 32 + 32 lambdas + ~9 genuinely shared = 233. The arithmetic closes exactly.

THE CONTROL THAT SETTLES IT. Three programs, 32 Enum.find call sites each:
  32 different lambdas   x > i          3.23s   7846 settles   233 execs   231 cone members
  32 IDENTICAL lambdas   x > 2          3.23s   7846 settles   233 execs   231 cone members
  1 shared lambda bound to a variable   0.35s   1283 settles    16 execs    14 cone members
Byte-identical lambda bodies cost EXACTLY the same as different ones, to the digit. So the fanout keys on lambda IDENTITY (source position), not on anything semantic. And the shared-lambda program costs exactly what ONE call site costs (16 executables, same as n=1).

9.2x wall clock. 14.6x executables. 6.1x product settles.

MECHANISM, still live at HEAD -- World::canonical_activation_key (world.rs:1745):
    if !recursive { return key; }
The fz-y6w convergence_collapse, which is exactly what merges equivalent evidence, runs ONLY for recursive functions. A NON-recursive shared library function is keyed by PRECISE evidence, and the arrow carries the closure brand, so it is specialized once per distinct closure value that reaches it. Confirmed in the activations dump -- two call sites, two arrows:
    Enum.find/2([int], (a1_p0) -> a1_r#65closure[])
    Enum.find/2([int], (a1_p0) -> a1_r#67closure[])
This is the same root fz-f98.5's 2026-06-25 investigation named; this ticket is the minimal general reproduction of it, outside the enum_take_drop_split context, and unblocked by f98.9/f98.10.

DO NOT ASSUME THE FIX IS "STOP SPECIALIZING". The specializations are NOT byte-identical copies: diffing fn66's four backend bodies (after normalising ids) leaves real differences in value layouts -- carrier Absent vs ValueRef, repr RawAtom vs ValueRef. Specialization per closure is also what buys direct dispatch and the closure_allocs = 0 pins the enum fixtures hold. Establish FIRST whether those layout differences are load-bearing or incidental; if incidental, that is itself a finding (schedule-dependent layouts). The target is sharing when the closures are equivalent FOR THE CALLEE'S PURPOSES, not deleting specialization.

PRIORITY vs fz-zg4. Do this FIRST. fz-zg4 (whole-program demand cone) is worth ~13% -- 350ms of 2.69s on enum_predicate_search. This is worth 9x, AND it shrinks fz-zg4's own problem: the demand cone drops from 231 members to 14 in the shared-lambda control, because cone size is downstream of executable count. Fixing the cone first means fixing it against an input that is 15x larger than it needs to be.

CHECKS: samebody_32 executables approach shared_32's; the ladder's exec/site approaches 1 (the lambda) rather than 7; enum fixture allocation goldens (closure_allocs, struct_allocs) unchanged; lib + matrix green.

comments.text:
DEFINITIVE CHARACTERIZATION -- the collapse road is OPEN, with exactly one named leak between here and the merge. Every claim below was established by a probe at HEAD and every probe is reverted (tree clean, guards green). This supersedes the year-old fz-f98.5 solution-space map, which was measured against machinery that no longer exists.

=== WHAT THE BRAND BUYS TODAY (measured, not assumed) ===
Named the per-site chain in find_4 (FNNAME probe + backend dump):
  Enum.find/2, Enum.find/3, reduce_while/3 x3 modules  -- x4 each, PURE PASS-THROUGH: none of them ever calls the closure
  #lambda enum.fz:5039-5131 (the wrapper find/3 builds) -- x4, the ONLY closure caller, and its ClosureCall has target=None (indirect by construction)
  reduce_while_cont/3 (recursive core)                  -- x1: ALREADY MERGED across all four brands by the fz-y6w collapse
So the specialized copies do not even buy a direct call at the invoke site. The recursive core is the standing existence proof that one executable can receive four brands through one input and stay green.

=== THE MULTI-BRAND TYPING MACHINERY IS READY ===
RESOLVE probe: callable_value_clauses enumerates brand UNIONS fine -- Some(2) for (#65|#67), Some(3) for a nested 3-way union inside reduce_while_cont. The year-old attempt-2 blocker (convergence_class collapsing is_pure_callable -> fun_top, erasing callable surfaces, 10 capture regressions) is GONE: fz-f98.14.10.2 replaced fun_top with resolvable addressed surface vars.

=== RE-RAN THE BLANKET COLLAPSE AT HEAD (E-A: drop the !recursive gate) ===
- find_1: WORKS, correct output, same 16 executables as today. shared_32: unchanged.
- find_2 and up: fails on ONE artifact guard, not ten capture tests:
    public closure callsite 0 settled return disagrees with its semantic result type: settled=:false | :true  semantic=any
  The callsite summary correctly enumerated BOTH targets (CCALL probe: public=true targets=2); only the VALUE-TYPING path earned any.

=== THE LEAK, TRACED END TO END ===
1. The wrapper's ActivationInputs under E-A accumulate a poisoned evidence row: [:nil, a1, int, :nil] -- a BARE ADDRESS VAR in the closure-capture column (EVIDENCE probe). Cumulative joins never retract, so one var row degrades the joined column to any at the callable use ([[unknown-is-not-none]]).
2. resolve_closure_call(callee=any) -> callable_value_clauses=None -> earns any (semantic.rs:1464). The four any-rounds in the RESOLVE log are exactly the post-poison rounds.
3. VARROW probe on conclude_activation_input_contributions caught the contributor red-handed: job=AnalyzeActivation(reduce_while_cont) -> wrapper [:nil, a1, int, :nil]. The RECURSIVE core's analysis publishes its own collapsed-key view (address var) as evidence to its callee.
4. CONTROL: with the gate restored (today's world), the SAME probe shows NO bare-var row anywhere -- fn182 contributes only precise branded rows. The leak is CREATED by collapsing the non-recursive callers; it is not pre-existing.
5. Falsified along the way: seeding was NOT the leak (seed_activation does contribute key params as evidence -- a latent hazard of the same class -- but skipping var seeds did not remove the poison row).

=== THE FIX SHAPE (two coupled parts, in order) ===
(a) An analysis running over a collapsed activation must not PUBLISH var-typed slots as activation-input evidence. A slot known only as an address var is not-yet-known, not a value; contribute the instantiated evidence or withhold the column. Detection is mechanical: the VARROW probe (log any contributed row containing a bare var in conclude_activation_input_contributions) plus the artifact settled-vs-semantic guard that already catches the downstream disagreement. seed_activation's key-params contribution belongs to the same rule.
(b) With (a) in place, extend the convergence collapse to non-recursive keys (drop the gate, or scope it to callable-carrying slots). Expected effect, bounded by the measured shared-lambda control: find_32 from 233 executables / 3.2s to ~16 / ~0.35s; per-site marginal cost from 7 executables to 1.
Guardrails: the artifact disagreement guard, the capture-surface suite, the enum fixture alloc pins (closure_allocs=0), lib+matrix.

REPRODUCER: 2 call sites suffice (find_2 in the ladder scripts). All probes are 5-line eprintlns recorded in the fz-6gb investigation; re-derive with: EVIDENCE (analyze_activation entry), VARROW (conclude_activation_input_contributions), RESOLVE (resolve_closure_call entry), CCALL (materialize_closure_call_edge).

ARC STATE (branch fz-6gb/brand-blind-library-keying, uncommitted): the keying model is BUILT and the win is measured; completion is BLOCKED by a pre-existing wrong-code bug in the callable-boundary return plane that the merge makes deterministic -- fz-f98.14.11, which now has a full mechanism trace (see the comment there).

WHAT IS IMPLEMENTED AND GREEN:
1. Evidence-not-key in the callsite-summary rebuild (semantic.rs ~1098): the rebuild reconstructed a closure target's capture prefix from target.activation.inputs() -- THE KEY -- and splices surface args on. Under any collapsed key that publishes key-language address vars as activation-input evidence (the poison row [:nil, a1, int, :nil] traced earlier). Now reads target.activation_inputs (the recorded evidence). Also a collapse: deletes the double key-read.
2. Interp construction encoder (ir_interp/backend.rs direct_callable_value): consumes the callable descriptor's capture_lanes like native does. CRITICAL SUBTLETY, learned by breaking the reduce family and re-fixing: extra lanes = capture_lanes.len() - sum(structural widths); a width-0 capture takes an extra lane (reading env) only while extras remain; otherwise it MUST be skipped WITHOUT reading the env -- a fully-erased capture's value is legitimately unbound.
3. The keying model: calls_closures fact co-produced with Recursive by DeriveRecursive; canonical_activation_key for non-recursive functions erases closure LITERALS from Ignore-masked slots via Types::erase_transported_closure_identities (value-language, no address vars, data untouched) UNLESS the body consumes callable identity. CONSUMPTION = calls through a callable (ClosureCall tail) OR constructs a lambda (Lambda step) OR IS a capture-holding lambda (capture_params non-empty -- identity is transitive through capture chains; learned from Enum.each's bridge lambda which only FORWARDS its capture to each_step).
4. Intent test compiler2_same_shape_lambda_literals_share_the_library_chain: green, both lanes, matches the Elixir oracle; marginal cost per site = own lambda + the two identity-consuming splits (+3), transporters shared.
5. Both design pins that failed under the year-old blanket collapse are green under this model: keeps_distinct_direct_callable_executables (direct dispatch per capture identity) and rendered_closure arity.

MEASURED WIN at this state: find_32 ladder 233 -> 47 executables, 7846 -> 1865 settles, 3.3s -> 0.84s, demand cone 231 -> 46.

THE BLOCKER (all remaining reds are one family): merging a transporter defers callable resolution from the call boundary (where values are bare FnRefs and the absent-return boundaries work) to DEEPER consumption points, where the return-lane plane conflation of fz-f98.14.11 produces wrong native code. Frontier: lib compiler2_opaque_callable_each_uses_an_absent_return_boundary (SIGABRT), compiler2_{interp,jit}_preserves_range_reduce3_halt_and_suspend; matrix enum_reduce_suspend x3, enum_take_drop_split x3, opaque_fn_each_absent_return run+build (interp lane of that fixture PASSES).

BISECTED REPRODUCER for the SIGABRT: erasing run/1 ALONE (mapper=each_a|each_b union through run into Enum.each) aborts after the first iteration; erasing the reduce/3 transporter alone is fine. Do not re-derive: prints "1" then fz_closure_get_capture_atom on word 0xfffff0007fc00000 (an f64 NaN -- an unwritten return lane) index=1.

ORDER OF WORK: fz-f98.14.11 first (it now has a deterministic reproducer and mechanism), then this branch's suites go green, then PR.

title: Each distinct lambda literal drags a private copy of every shared library function it reaches: 32 identical lambdas cost 9x wall clock and 15x executables
